Because \(E\) lies on \(AD\) and \(F\) lies on \(BC\), we can denote the length of \(AD\) and \(BC\) as \(s\) (the side length of the square). The distance from \(B\) to the midpoint of \(EF\) forms a right triangle with legs of length \(30\) and \(15\), and the hypotenuse of this triangle is \(s/2\). So we can use the Pythagorean theorem to find \(s\):

Simplifying the right-hand side:
